Alex — great context, and congrats on the upcoming launch. Below is a concise proposal to map monthly commits to tiered per-token pricing and step-up windows that align with your beta and launch cadence. Willing to iterate on numbers once procurement shares target commit levels.

Proposal (high level):
- Baseline monthly commit: 100M tokens (12-month term) -> $0.0016 / token (committed rate)
- Step-up window A (month 3): increase to 200M -> blended rate for months 3–5: $0.00135 / token if commit increased is accepted by month 2
- Step-up window B (month 6): target 350M -> discount to $0.00110 / token for incremental usage above 300M
- Overages: 5% surcharge on any consumption above agreed monthly cap unless a short-term burst add-on is purchased

Seasonality protection: offer optional 'launch buffer' credit equal to 10% of monthly commit for the first two months post-launch to cover unpredictability.

Next steps: I can produce an SOW draft with a table of month-by-month commit steps and a sample billing schedule. Monica — can you attach a sample SOW and ramp sheet?

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik and Monica — the SOW and workbook look good. Procurement has two asks: 1) Can we get a firmer guarantee on the step-up mechanics so our finance team can forecast liability? Specifically: will the month 3 increase be treated as a hard commit (billing from day 1 of month 3) or an option to convert on notice? 2) We prefer caps vs. surcharges — instead of a 5% surcharge on overages, can we include a capped overage that escalates by $0.0005 / token after 120% of the cap?

Also, our CFO is sensitive to blended-rate calculations for mid-month step-ups; can you provide a worked example where a step-up triggers on day 10 of a 30-day month?

Alex

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@brightgrid.ai>, Procurement <procurement@brightgrid.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-27T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Volume tiers + launch seasonality — proposal and activation windows

Alex — good questions. Clarifications below and an attached worked example included.

1) Step-up mechanics: by default we treat a planned step-up as an option that must be exercised by a 7-day notice before the step month starts; once exercised, the increased commit becomes a hard commit and billing begins at day 1 of that new month. Alternatively, for launches where you want automatic activation, we can include an "auto-escalate" clause that increases commit automatically when observed rolling-7-day usage exceeds 85% of the next-tier target for 5 consecutive days. That option requires an additional buffer credit to be negotiated.

2) Overages: we can replace the 5% surcharge with a capped overage band: up to 120% of monthly cap incurs a $0.0009 / token overage; 120–150% incurs $0.0012 / token; above 150% we charge standard pay-as-you-go rate. This preserves predictability while allowing for short bursts.

3) Worked example: attached workbook shows prorated billing when a step-up is requested mid-month (day 10). In short: charges are prorated by daily active commit split and blended for the invoice. Example: month with 30 days, base commit 100M increases to 200M on day 10 -> days 1–9 billed at base rate for 100M, days 10–30 billed at committed rate for 200M; blended invoice rate calculated across total tokens consumed.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll push a revised SOW to DocuSign for signature and loop in Finance for any prepayment discussion.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments referenced: brightgrid_pricing_worked_example.xlsx

From: Procurement <procurement@brightgrid.ai>

Subject: Re: Volume tiers + launch seasonality — proposal and activation windows

Karthik / Monica — procurement reviewed and has one additional request before legal and finance sign-off: can you add an early termination protection that allows BrightGrid to revert to a lower committed tier (with 60 days' notice) if actual post-launch retention metrics fall below 40% of forecast for two consecutive months? In that case, we propose a modest unwind fee equal to 10% of the remaining monthly commit value.

Also please include a clause for quarterly usage reviews where either party can request rate re-opener if sustained variance >20% vs. forecast.

Procurement — BrightGrid

- Overages: adopt the capped overage bands (up to 120% at $0.0009 / token; 120–150% at $0.0012 / token).
- Early termination protection: BrightGrid may down-tier with 60 days' notice if post-launch retention <40% for two consecutive months; unwind fee set at 10% of remaining monthly commit value.
